note.text: Cameroon’s climates vary with latitude, seasonal air circulation, distance from the sea and relief. The coast is generally very wet; parts of the southern interior have a bimodal rainfall pattern with two wetter seasons. Western highlands are cooler than nearby lowlands and relief modifies rainfall. Northern tropical landscapes have a stronger dry-season contrast, becoming more semi-arid towards the Far North. School names include equatorial, monsoon or Cameroonian, Guinean, Sudanian, Sahelian and highland variants; labels must be linked to their actual characteristics rather than treated as identical schemes.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to compare coastal southern-interior highland and northern regimes and explain how location and relief modify them. Builds on: global seasonal climates and Cameroon’s position, relief and drainage. Leads to: regional vegetation and soil patterns.

sections.heading: Follow the local example or model
sections.text: Compare a wet coast near Douala, the southern plateau around Yaoundé, the western highlands and the northern plains. A hill’s windward side and sheltered side can differ, and altitude affects temperature. The supplied annual rainfall figures are fictional examples. They demonstrate a difference in totals, not a forecast or the precise mean for a real town. One national average would conceal important regional contrasts.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Describe temperature and rainfall amount and timing before applying a climate label. Distinguish weather on a particular day from climate over a longer reference period. State the station and period when using real records. A broad north-south tendency does not eliminate local variation or establish a land-use recommendation by itself.

questions.prompt: Two invented annual station records give {coast} mm for a wet coastal site and {north} mm for a drier northern site. How much greater is the coastal total? These are teaching data, not observed town averages.

misconceptions.explain: That combines the records rather than comparing them.
That reports the full coastal total, not its excess.
That repeats the northern total instead of calculating the difference.

solution: Compare totals for the same period and unit.
Difference = {coast} − {north} = {answer} mm. Annual totals do not reveal every seasonal detail.
